name: Kadhi Pakora
steps: Whisk curd, gram flour, water, turmeric and salt until smooth with no flour lumps.
Heat half the ghee in a deep pan, sizzle cumin and fenugreek briefly, then lower the heat.
Pour in the curd mixture gradually while stirring. Bring to a gentle boil, stirring continuously so the flour does not settle.
Reduce heat and simmer for 25–30 minutes, stirring often, until the gram flour is cooked and the kadhi is smooth and pourable.
For pakora, thinly slice the extra onion and mix with the extra gram flour, coriander and salt. Add the extra water gradually to form a thick coating batter.
Heat frying oil to 170°C and drop small spoonfuls carefully. Fry for 4–5 minutes until golden and cooked through, then drain.
Heat remaining ghee, add dried chilli, turn off the heat and stir in chilli powder briefly. Pour this tempering over the kadhi.
Finish with coriander and serve hot. Add boiling water if it thickens excessively during simmering.
Add pakoras to the finished kadhi and simmer for 3–4 minutes to soften slightly. Serve hot; add them later if you prefer a firmer texture.
tips: Measure and prepare all components before cooking, then taste and adjust seasoning before serving.
notes: Quantities are for four adult portions. Cooking times are estimates; use the doneness checks in each step. Ingredient costs use sample rates and exclude unpriced items.
